content.content:
# Piton fluency

Piton is a declarative, whitespace-structured language for describing agentic
skills, agents, commands, and reference documents. It has no runtime: it
compiles to data (JSON, YAML) or, through a framework, to Markdown. Source
files use the `.pi` extension.

## Syntax

```piton
// A comment. Comments are line-only.
myVariable: 42                       // a number
myString: Strings are unquoted       // a string
myQuoted: "false"                    // quoting forces a string
myTyped:: string:: number: 42        // constraints, first match wins

myList:
    - one
    - two
myInlineList: [one, two, three]

name: spec-prompts-include-piton-fluency
description: Any prompt about the spec (subagents, workflows) must embed output of `piton claude --print-prompt`
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Any prompt sent regarding a spec (in ./spec) — e.g. to subagents via Agent or Workflow — must inherently include the Piton fluency text retrieved by running `piton claude --print-prompt`.

**Why:** The user asked for it; the spec is written in Piton (.pi), and agents without that fluency primer misread the syntax.

**How to apply:** Before delegating spec-related work, run `piton claude --print-prompt` and embed its full output in the agent prompt (fetch it fresh rather than paraphrasing). Related: ./spec is read-only, code lives in ./src.
